business: MemoryWorks (company memory and pre-action briefings for engineering teams and their AI agents)
target: Engineering leaders (CTOs, eng managers, platform/SRE leads) at software companies with 10 to 500 engineers whose teams already run AI coding agents on production repos
where: Online, B2B SaaS / open-source developer tool, mostly US and Europe

segments.name: Startup CTO or founding engineer (10 to 50 engineers), signs the card themselves
Engineering manager at a scale-up (50 to 300 engineers), has a team tooling budget
Platform or SRE lead at a larger company (300+ engineers), needs security review and procurement
Small agency or consultancy lead (under 10 engineers)

behaviours.name: AI-agent early adopter
behaviours.how: Runs Claude Code or Cursor agents on real repos daily and is actively looking for ways to make them safer.

behaviours.name: Incident-scarred
behaviours.how: Recently had an outage repeat one the team already wrote a postmortem for, and is still annoyed about it.

behaviours.name: Build-it-ourselves
behaviours.how: Default reaction to a dev tool is 'we could build that with a vector DB and an MCP server'.

behaviours.name: Security gatekeeper
behaviours.how: Will not connect Slack or GitHub to a new vendor without SOC 2, a DPA and a security questionnaire.

behaviours.name: Tool-fatigued
behaviours.how: Already pays for Notion, Confluence or Glean, PagerDuty and more; resists every new tool.

behaviours.name: Bottom-up trialer
behaviours.how: Signs up free, tries it on one repo, and only pays if the team keeps using it after two weeks.

behaviours.name: Budget-constrained
behaviours.how: Has to justify every per-seat tool to finance with a concrete saving.

objections: We already have Glean, Notion AI or Confluence search for this
Connecting our Slack and GitHub to a small startup is a security risk
Our agents don't do anything risky enough to need a briefing yet
Who keeps the memory accurate? It will go stale like our wiki
I could build this with a vector DB and an MCP server in a week
Another per-seat tool is a hard sell to finance
Will this company still exist in two years?
My engineers won't change how they work to feed another tool
habits: you run Claude Code or Cursor agents on your company's repos most days
you were paged twice last quarter for something that had happened before
your team's postmortems live in a Google Drive folder nobody opens
you sit in a weekly architecture review where the same questions come back
you approve or block every new vendor that touches source code
you spend part of every week answering 'who owns this service?' in Slack
